title: THE MOON IS BACK. (nobody's fasting this time.)
format: carousel, 4 slides at 1080x1440: S1 video loop 10.0 s (frame 0 = the cover = the grid tile, soft baked foley in AAC), S2 video loop 6.0 s (silent), S3 still (the studio photograph), S4 still (the end card). The brief's S4, the worn photograph 04.jpg, is dropped (see deviations and owner_questions)
date: Fri 20 Nov 2026 (eve of Tulsi Vivah and the first muhurat; never dated on any image)
caption:
The moon is back over the terrace. Nobody's fasting this time: it is wedding season, and the buffet opens at nine.

The Heartbead Bracelet takes both lights: mirror-polished rhodium plated beads, about 6 mm, for the moon, and at the front a gold tone toggle and one puffed gold tone heart, about 15 mm, for the string lights. Cool and quiet, warm only at the front. ₹1,299.

Take 2 pieces for 10% off or 3 for 20% off. The bag applies BUY2 or BUY3 for you.

first_comment: See you on the terrace. Every piece arrives in our blush box · free insured shipping · COD available #NairaFlore #WeddingSeason #WeddingGuest #DemiFineJewellery #NairaPetite
alt_text: An illustrated pink Art Deco terrace at night under a string of warm lights, a bright moon in the plum sky with a thin cloud across its lower edge, and a pink paper lantern at the left. The words THE MOON IS BACK, 'nobody's fasting this time.' On the parapet's ledge lies a bracelet of mirror-bright grey beads with a gold-tone toggle and one puffed gold-tone heart hanging over the edge of the wall. The cloud drifts off the moon, moonlight runs bead by bead along the strand to the clasp, the heart catches one warm glint, and a second cloud drifts back across the moon. A brass plate on the parapet carries the Naira wordmark.

On a deep aubergine ground, a close photograph of the bracelet's front: two runs of mirror-bright grey rhodium-plated beads that fall away into the dark at either end, the gold-tone toggle bar and ring, and the puffed gold-tone heart hanging from the ring. A cool light passes along the beads and then a warm glint crosses the heart, under the words COOL AND QUIET. and '(the only warmth comes at the front.)', with '(shown larger.)' at the foot.

Studio photograph of the Heartbead Bracelet lying on a cream plaster block, its strand of mirror-bright grey beads on top and the gold-tone toggle and puffed heart hanging over the block's front edge, framed in a thin gold line on aubergine, with the lines: rhodium plated beads, about 6 mm · a puffed gold tone heart, about 15 mm, and: the toggle closes at the front.

End card on rose plaster: a brass plate with the Naira wordmark, then TERRACE · CENTRE, HEARTBEAD BRACELET, rhodium plated · one gold tone heart, ₹1,299, 'one warm thing on the terrace.', nairaflore.com, and every piece arrives in our blush box · free insured shipping · COD available.
sound: Slide 1 carries its own very soft baked foley (peak -23 dBFS, mean -44 dB): a faint night-breeze bed built periodic over exactly 10.0 s so the loop seam is continuous (seam step 0.00014), a very soft high shimmer under the moonlight's run (2.55-4.95 s, panned right to left with it) and a faint high chime at 5.2 s as the heart takes its glint. Optional in-app: a spacious night instrumental (santoor or soft strings) from the Instagram audio library, no vocals, ducked under the foley. Slide 2 silent.
deviations: FOUR SLIDES, NOT FIVE (director r2 fix 2). The brief's S4, assets/shopify/heartbead-bracelet/04.jpg (worn on the wrist), is dropped. Next to the studio photographs 01.jpg and 05.jpg (which the cut-outs and S3 come from), its clasp is different: the toggle bar has ball ends where the real bar is a plain flat-ended cylinder, and the small spacer bead and link before the ring are missing. Its beads also read near-black hematite, not the listing's 'mirror bright' rhodium that is 'cool and quiet'. So it fails the system's rule that every image is checked against the listing photograph, toggle included, and is very likely a render (the same doubt the brief raises about P8's and P9's worn slides). 02.jpg is not substituted: at 640 px it would have to be upscaled. The end card moves from s05 to s04 (s04.html, re-rendered: pixel-identical to the old s05.jpg). The old s04.* files are deleted. See owner_questions.

Placement is the world's (world README deviation 4): the studio cut-out (CUT-V3-04, 567 x 576, a high-angle shot) at 0.66 with its box at tile (540, 774) (fix pass: was 786). The back run now tops out at tile y 782, 18 px over the sky line at 800, a deliberate silhouette of beads resting at the ledge's far edge rather than a tangent on it. The toggle ring and heart hang over the coping. Native scale would stand the loop up into the sky. About 135 px wide in the grid, not the brief's ~217.

THE MOON IS MOVED FROM THE BAY, not from world.js (director fix 8; the world lead was not reachable from this session and shared files are off limits). p11.js finds the world's .w-moon and sets its top ABSOLUTELY to the tile y 200 box (disc ~212-440), so the far wire crosses the upper cap ~30 px inside the rim and the bulbs hang in front of the moon. Because it is absolute it becomes a no-op once world.js line 472 (the moonEl line) reads `top:${300 + 200 - 90}px`. For the world lead: make that change in world.js and update 'y 230-470' to 'y 200-440' in render/v3/README.md (lines 71 and 246). Only P11's tile shows the moon, and the moon is hidden whenever P11 is not lit, so P11's CLOSED state and the neighbours are unchanged. FINAL WORLD (world.js 21:32): that line still reads `top:${300 + 230 - 90}px`, so the bay's absolute top is what places the moon in every render of this pass, and the handover stands.

Both cut-outs re-matted with the house's anti-aliased edge (p11/_build/rematte.py, the recipe of brushed-gold-huggies/00-aa: contour smoothed at 4x, eroded 0.5 px, box-downsampled; RGB byte-identical, alpha never higher) into p11/assets/heartbead-v3-05-aa.png and heartbead-00-aa.png: both originals have a binary 0/255 alpha that stair-steps at 1:1. Slide 2 alone uses heartbead-00-aa-s2.png, its alpha choked 1 px more (grey erosion, 3x3 cross, RGB byte-identical) for the aubergine ground. The broader beige band inside the left-run beads is each mirror bead's own reflection of the studio plinth, inside the silhouette, and is left as photographed (never recoloured). The bay places its own (b.cut only knows cutouts/ keys); NV.CUTS and cutouts/ are untouched.

Masks (p11/_build/fixmasks.py, originals in p11/_build/orig-assets/): every gold-mask component except the largest is the toggle's reflection inside a mirror bead, so it is moved into the beads mask with its 2 px moat (slide 1: one 472 px island in bead 15; slide 2: three islands of 583, 593 and 745 px). The cool lights now cover them, and the warm gold light no longer tints them brown. Slide 2's heart mask is cut along the groove where the bail tab meets the heart (native x ~148-226, y ~760-838, feathered 1 px), so the warm glint is on the heart's body only, never on the bail or jump ring.

The cool moonlight on the beads is a soft reflection of the moon on each bead's upper right (a spot inset from the bead's edge, screen #F4F2F0, painted back to front, masked to the beads' alpha), not a rim along each bead's top: the rim version (and a top-light gradient) read as a white outline round every bead at 1:1, a halo. The run's sheen is a specular point on that same moon reflection (r .55 of the bead at (cx+.30r, cy-.36r), stops .35/.10), never a disc over the whole bead: the disc frosted each bead flat, which reads as pearl.

Contact shadows are traced from the piece's own silhouette (multiply, warm plum): on the ledge a tight one (blur 1.1, 0.6/2.2 px) and a soft one (blur 5, 1.5/6 px); below the ledge's arris, where the toggle and heart hang over the coping face and the parapet, a softer one thrown 2/10 px, as an object a few mm off the wall. The brief's single ellipse sat under the front beads only and left the loop pasted on.

Sparkles are 24 px (the post says 14 px; the system's range is 22-28), with a 1.4 white core and a .7 glow. They sit on each bead's moon reflection, not on the photo's own studio highlight, where an already-white #F4F2F0 star could not be seen. There are eight of them, 0.25 s apart and 0.5 s each (never more than two on screen), on beads 10, 12, 14, 16, 17, 18, 19 and 20 of the strand.

The moonlight's run is also carried by the beads themselves: each of twelve beads, from the back of the loop on the moon's side, down the right and along the front to the ring, takes the specular point in turn (a 0.23 s Gaussian) with the sparkles. The run reaches the ring at about 4.7 s and the heart answers with its glint at 5.2 s.

LIGHT-BAND TRAVEL (beyond the director's list; the timing of every beat is unchanged). At 120% -> -20% of their oversized backgrounds, the glints and the sweep sat off the piece for about two thirds of each pass. Measured on lossless frames: the S1 glint was on the heart ~0.1 s (3 frames), the S2 warm glint ~0.15 s, and the S2 cool line crossed every bead in ~0.25 s at about 85 px a frame. With the thinner bands the director asked for, that strobes. Each band now travels from just off its masked area to just past it (p11/_build/bandrange.py: S1 glint 84.8% -> 18.4%, S2 cool 89.8% -> 14.3%, S2 warm 83.1% -> 16.6%) on the kit's sine in-out rather than the strong bezier in-out. Measured: the S1 glint crosses the heart 5.30-5.70 s, the S2 warm glint 2.55-3.25 s, and the S2 cool line the left run 0.80-1.15 s and the right run 1.30-1.65 s. Each band enters and leaves invisibly, so the loops still match end to end.

The wisp is a moonlit cloud, not the brief's 8% ivory ellipse: a mauve-grey body (rgba(196,178,196,.30), blur 14) with a cream streak, a tail and a filament, centred at y 402 (with the moon, was 432) so it crosses the moon's foot. At 8% ivory it was invisible on the night sky and over the cream disc, so 'the wisp clears' could not read. A mid-tone body lightens the sky and veils the moon a little, so it reads in front of the disc. At rest its footprint is x 471-1018, y 359-453 (nothing reaches a tile edge in the world). Its band holds two copies 1300 px apart (was 1100: the second copy then parked at c 135, on the kandil's own x, and turned into a coral bar through the halo for 6.4 s of the loop), and the non-moving .p-wisp container carries a fixed mask, transparent over x 0-300 and ramping to opaque at 440: while the moon is clear (3.2-6.0 s) slide 1 parks the band at +620 (final review fix 1; at +500 the wisp's left tail stayed caught on the right pole, x ~971-1080, for the whole 'moon clear' beat): the leading copy (x 1091-1638) is then wholly past the slide's right edge, the second copy parks at c 55 with its right end at x ~338, in the mask's ramp, where it adds at most 2 levels, and the incoming wisp forms out of the sky between x 300 and 440 from about 6.2 s. The mask rasterises the wisp in its own layer, so frame 0 differs from the previous build by at most 3 levels inside the wisp's footprint (mean 0.006); the world tile and the cover carry the same pixels as frame 0.

The halo's 18 -> 22% is an extra layer in this bay (the world's halo is shared and untouched; this layer's box follows the moon to top 110). It follows how much of the moon a wisp covers, and so do the beads' moon reflections (frame-0 level .82 -> 1), so the clearing visibly lights the strand and the second wisp dims it back for the seam.

The warm string light falls on all the gold (strongest on the heart, a little on the toggle): the toggle is the same gold tone, and a warm heart beside a cold toggle read as a mismatch. The one warm glint is on the heart only, as briefed: ivory #FFF7E6 at .30/.45/.30 over 47-53%, a narrow line travelling over gold that leaves the heart gold.

Slide 1's ambient clock is offset 9.05 s so frame 0 shows the kandil's flower window to the street, the same pose as P10's cover; every ambient period (10.0 s turn, 5.0 s sway and bulbs) divides the loop.

Slide 2: the macro cut-out's two cut ends (the photograph's frame cut the strand at its top and its right) fall away into the dark under a radial falloff on the piece (#000 to 70%, .5 at 80%, 0 at 86%), and since the director's r2 review also under two directional ramps on nested wrappers (the masks multiply): #endR alpha 1 at slide x 740 to 0 at 790 and #endT alpha 0 at slide y 545 to 1 at 600, each a smoothstep in five stops rather than a straight line, so neither ramp has a shoulder that could read as an edge. The director specified them over y 915-1015 and x 220-430. #endT is drawn full width: above y 545 everything outside x 220-430 has already been cleared by the radial (measured: the piece's only alpha there, x 430-503 / y 446-476, is at 0 after the radial), so the result is the same. #endR is drawn full height, because the last full bead runs down to y 1075. Stopping the ramp at y 1015 would cut a horizontal line through that bead, and nothing else of the piece lies right of x 740. One addition, #endH: a hole round (803, 962), clear to 27 px and solid from 34 px, removes what the ramp left of the half bead's lit left rim above the last bead (up to 10 levels over the ground at x 777-783 / y 956-974). The hole stays clear of the last bead's own disc: the largest change inside it is 1 level. All of this sits over a low lilac pool of light behind the front, with a soft drop shadow. The cool sweep is a thin specular line (#F4F2F0 .28/.42/.28 over 46-54%), so every bead keeps its dark mirror reflections while it crosses; a wide band had whitened them to pearl.

'(shown larger.)' kept on slide 2: at 0.75 the beads measure about 17 px/mm (life size on a phone is about 16), though by the listing's 15 mm the heart measures about 12 px/mm. The photograph's own bead-to-heart ratio (1 : 1.75) does not match the listing's 6 mm and 15 mm, so the conservative note stays.

Bay OPENING(t) (the close-up story, a nominal 3.6 s; no slide of this post uses it, because slide 1 starts lit): the C-OUTLINE draws at ~960 px/s, the photograph develops over 0.9 s, and the outline retracts over 0.7 s with a 0.6 s overlap, fading to 25% as the photo arrives. A full cream line hugging the developed photograph read as a sticker border. The outline follows the new Y.

A gibbous moon (the true phase on 20 Nov is ~83% lit, waxing) was tried as a soft terminator over the world's disc and rejected: it left a ghost ring of the full disc and read as an eclipse. The moon stays the world's full disc. 'Almost-full' lives in the concept, not on the image, so slide 1's alt text now says 'a bright moon' (the brief's alt text says 'an almost-full moon'; restore it if the owner wants the phase in the text).

ECD FIX 4, part 2, the kandil's jumps inside the loop (the same kit fault, mid-loop here): scanning the band on all 300 frames (p11/_work/ecd-fix: P2's detector, plus a test that the band's points run in increasing azimuth) found six one-frame jumps, viewed at 3x (band-mp4-old.png). Near each face-on pose (theta = 0 mod 60 deg, within ~1.15 deg) both side facets pass kit/kandil.js's cos(psi) > -0.02, and its chain, which sorts the segments by their min x, ties. At frames 28, 78, 128, 178 and 228 the band's left half bent into a V (side -> back -> front). At 278 it doubled back from the front to the left-back corner, a gold zigzag across the lantern. At 29, 79, 129, 179, 229 and 279 the right stub dropped. On the encoded loop these were the lantern's five largest steps: 1.21 / 1.21 into 278 / 279, 1.00 / 1.03 into 128 / 129, 0.97 into 229, against a 0.72 median. The kit is shared and not this post's to edit, so world/bays/p11.js gains kandilBand(b, ms), called from a new tick(h, ms) after the kit's tick. It draws the band from the kit's own vertices and visibility test with the same arithmetic, so the same d to the digit, chained in facet order round the front from left to right, and writes only when the kit's chain differs. Checked on all 300 frames: it changes exactly frames 28, 29, 78, 79, 128, 129, 178, 179, 228, 229, 278, 279. The other 288 bands are the same string, and every band now runs in strictly increasing azimuth. Lossless frames 0, 1, 2 are pixel-identical to before. On the new encode the lantern steps into those frames are 0.65-0.81 (were 0.86-1.21), and its largest step in the loop is 0.88 at frame 244, an ordinary step of the turn. The tick is a no-op once the kit chains by azimuth. Left for the kit: every bay's kandil still bends at its own near-face-on frames.
